title: Christ's grace frees from due penalty; cross bears curse (Isa 53)
source_text: VI. Utrumque per Christi gratiam tollitur. Et primo quidem certum est Christum eos qui ad ipsum serio confugiunt a poena peccato debita liberare, & in fidelibus ac poenitentibus solvere obligationem illam, qua, propter admissa peccata, aeternae mortis coram Deo rei sunt atque debitores. Quam gratiam Christus nobis meruit atque impetravit, dum, tanquam vas noster atque nostro nomine, poenas dirissimas in cruce pertulit, & pro nobis passus est, justus ipse pro injustis. Quo respectu dicitur peccata nostra pertulisse in corpore suo super lignum. Item nos redemisse de maledicto legis, dum factus est pro nobis maledictum. Juxta quod ab Isaia Propheta praedictum fuerat, Vulneratus est propter iniquitates nostras, attritus est propter scelera nostra. Omnes nos quasi oves erravimus, unusquisque in viam suam declinavit; & posuit Dominus in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum. Isa. 53. 5, 6.
pass_a_gloss: Both are taken away by Christ's grace. And first indeed it is certain that Christ frees those who seriously flee to him from the penalty due to sin, and in the faithful and penitent dissolves that obligation by which, because of sins committed, they are guilty and debtors of eternal death before God. Which grace Christ merited and obtained for us when, as our vessel and in our name, he bore the most dire penalties on the cross, and suffered for us, the just himself for the unjust. In which respect he is said to have borne our sins in his body on the tree. Likewise to have redeemed us from the curse of the law, when he was made a curse for us. According to what had been foretold by the Prophet Isaiah: He was wounded for our iniquities, bruised for our crimes. We all like sheep have gone astray, each turned to his own way; and the Lord laid on him the iniquity of us all (Isaiah 53:5-6).
pass_b_english: Christ's grace frees serious seekers from sin's due eternal-death obligation.
As our surety he bore cross-penalties—the just for the unjust—and redeemed from the law's curse (Isaiah 53:5-6).
